title: The Magic Art of the Great Humbug, part 3
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “I have come for my courage,” announced the Lion, entering the room.
“Very well,” answered the little man; “I will get it for you.”

He went to a cupboard and reaching up to a high shelf took down a square green bottle, the contents of which he poured into a green-gold dish, beautifully carved. Placing this before the Cowardly Lion, who sniffed at it as if he did not like it, the Wizard said:

“Well,” answered Oz, “if it were inside of you, it would be courage. You know, of course, that courage is always inside one; so that this really cannot be called courage until you have swallowed it. Therefore I advise you to drink it as soon as possible.”
The Lion hesitated no longer, but drank till the dish was empty.
“How do you feel now?” asked Oz.
“Full of courage,” replied the Lion, who went joyfully back to his friends to tell them of his good fortune.

Oz, left to himself, smiled to think of his success in giving the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman and the Lion exactly what they thought they wanted. “How can I help being a humbug,” he said, “when all these people make me do things that everybody knows can’t be done? It was easy to make the Scarecrow and the Lion and the Woodman happy, because they imagined I could do anything. But it will take more than imagination to carry Dorothy back to Kansas, and I’m sure I don’t know how it can be done.”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where did Oz keep the courage?
options: In a square green bottle on a high shelf
In a chest of drawers by the throne
In a golden pot covered with a plate
In the back room with the bran

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did he pour the contents into?
options: A green-gold dish, beautifully carved
A plain tin cup from the kitchen
The Tin Woodman's own oil-can
A bowl of thick green glass

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Lion first react to it?
options: He sniffed at it as if he did not like it
He drank it down at once without asking
He refused to come near the dish at all
He asked what such a drink had cost

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Lion say when asked how he felt?
options: Full of courage

Frightened still

Dorothy and her little dog Toto only

Nobody at all among them so far

The drink will not keep once it is poured out
It works only if taken before noon
The dish must be returned to the cupboard

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Oz say he cannot help being a humbug?
options: People ask him to do things everyone knows cannot be done
He was trained as a ventriloquist and cannot stop
The Witches would destroy him if he told the truth
His people would never believe the truth anyway

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why were the three so easy to satisfy?
options: They imagined he could do anything
They asked for very small things
They never checked what he gave them
They were afraid to complain

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does hesitated no longer mean?
options: He stopped holding back and acted
He refused to wait for an answer
He grew angry and spoke out
He asked one more question first

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: Three wishes granted by belief, and one that belief cannot solve

options: That he had come for his courage
That he no longer needed anything
That the Scarecrow had sent him
That he would not drink anything

options: All of it, till the dish was empty
Only a little, and left the rest
None at all
Half, and gave the rest to Toto

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Oz do when he was left alone?
options: Smiled to think of his success
Wept over his own dishonesty
Began at once to build a balloon
Sent for Dorothy immediately

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the Lion feel as he left?
options: Joyful, and eager to tell his friends

Angry at the taste of the drink

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
